name: Pennsylvania-class battleship
blurb: One of the older battleships, planned for Surigao Strait.
history:
The Pennsylvania class was two super-dreadnought battleships, Pennsylvania and Arizona, built for the U.S. Navy just before the First World War and armed with twelve 14-inch guns. Both were modernized between 1929 and 1931.

Both were at Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941: Arizona was sunk by a magazine explosion and became a memorial, while Pennsylvania, in dry dock, was only lightly damaged. After a refit she served mostly as a shore bombardment ship, and she was present at the Battle of Surigao Strait, the last battle between battleships, though she did not engage.
